description:
AI Engineer, AI/ML and Agent Harnessing (New Grad, 2027)
Location

Sunnyvale, CA

Employment Type

Full time

Location Type

On-site

Department

AI Research & Engineering

Compensation
$135K – $190K • Offers Equity
Overview
Application

The future of defense will be decided by those who field intelligent machines at scale. At Scout AI, we’re developing Fury, the first robotic foundation model for defense, to give U.S. forces overwhelming, adaptable, and autonomous power across every domain. Fury enables human operators to command fleets of robots through natural language, and empowers those machines to sense, decide, and act together as one. This mission will ask everything of us: urgency, precision, and relentless work.

The Role

We’re looking for a New Grad AI Engineer to work on the AI behind Fury. You’ll work on two connected problems: the models themselves, and the agent harness around them, which is the set of tools, data streams, and services that lets an AI agent get real work done on real systems.

This is a broad role. Depending on where you’re strongest, you might spend most of your time training and evaluating models, building agent harnesses and the services they depend on, or building the evals and data pipelines that show whether a change helped. Early on you’ll take well-scoped pieces of real systems, work next to senior engineers who review your code, and learn by shipping. As you get your footing, you’ll be expected to take on bigger pieces.

We want people who are at home with agents and models: prompting them, wiring them to data and tools, and noticing when their behavior is off. We also want solid software habits, like modular code and clean service boundaries, because an agent prototype that can’t grow into a real system isn’t much use to us.

We use AI coding tools and expect you to as well, but we think of them as a multiplier on skills you already have. You should be able to write, explain, and debug your own code without them.

We’re a startup. You’ll be moving fast, context-switching often, and helping shape the culture and process as we go. It’s a rare chance to come in early and help build the future of defense.

Responsibilities

Build and improve the agent harness, including the tools, context, and services agents use to work with data streams and real systems

Prototype new agent behaviors quickly, then turn the ones that work into modular, tested services

Train, fine-tune, and evaluate models for Fury, working with senior engineers and researchers

Build evals and datasets that show whether a model or agent change made things better or worse

Write Python tooling and data pipelines that support training, evaluation, and agent workloads

Read agent traces and model outputs to work out why something failed, then fix the cause

Work with the core software and Fury teams to connect agents to simulation, cloud, and onboard systems

Qualifications

BS or MS in computer science, machine learning, computer engineering, or a related field, completed or finishing by summer 2027

Proficient in Python from coursework, internships, research, or personal projects

Something you have built with models or agents and can explain end to end, such as a tool-using agent or a model you trained or fine-tuned

Keeps up with new models, agent frameworks, and research, and has opinions about what works

Picks up new tools quickly and asks for help early when stuck

Ability to write, debug, and explain complex code independently without relying on AI tools

Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

Passion about defense of the United States and its allies

May be expected to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

Nice to Have

Experience with PyTorch or a similar ML framework

Experience with LLM APIs or agent frameworks, including tool calling and multi-step agents

Experience building eval datasets or benchmarks for models or agents

Experience with vision-language models, reinforcement learning, or robotics simulation

Familiarity with game engines, simulation environments, or robotics middleware (such as ROS)

Why Join Scout

Work on the world’s most important frontier, ensuring U.S. and allied dominance in the age of intelligent machines

Be a core part of a team building the first defense-specific robotic foundation model

Collaborate with some of the top engineers in autonomy, AI, and national security

See your work deployed on real systems

Help define the future of intelligent defense systems

Backed by Draper Associates, Booz Allen Ventures, and other top investors

Benefits

Competitive Cash Compensation

Meaningful equity

Premium medical, dental, and vision plans with $0 paycheck contribution

401k with match

Competitive PTO and company holiday calendar

Catered lunch daily and fully stocked kitchen

EV charging

Relocation assistance (depending on role eligibility)
